questions.q: What runs inside the Driver Program?
options: Your actual code, along with the SparkContext/SparkSession that plans and coordinates the job
The physical data files themselves
Only the Cluster Manager's resource allocation logic
Nothing — the Driver Program is just a placeholder with no real function
questions.explain: The driver plans the work but doesn't do the heavy lifting itself — that's the executors' job.

questions.q: What does the Cluster Manager do?
options: Allocates machines and resources to a Spark job — this could be Spark's own standalone manager, Kubernetes, or YARN
Writes the Python code for the job
Runs the actual data transformations
Stores the final output files
questions.explain: It's the middleman between the driver and the actual worker machines.

options: The name of Spark's cluster manager
A type of file format
A synonym for the Driver Program
A process on a worker node that runs Tasks and can cache data in memory for reuse
questions.explain: Executors are where the actual computation happens, on the worker nodes.

questions.q: How does Spark's architecture implement data locality (from Lesson 29)?
options: Executors always run on a single, fixed machine regardless of data location
Data locality has no connection to Spark's actual architecture
The Driver Program physically copies all data to itself first
The Cluster Manager tries to place Executors on machines that already hold the relevant data, rather than moving data elsewhere
questions.explain: This is exactly the general idea from Lesson 29, implemented by a real architectural component.

questions.q: How does Spark's architecture implement fault tolerance (from Lesson 29)?
options: The Cluster Manager prevents any machine from ever failing
If any Worker Node fails, the entire Spark job is permanently lost with no recovery
If a Worker Node fails mid-job, the Driver reschedules that Executor's unfinished Tasks onto a different Worker Node
Fault tolerance is not actually possible in Spark's architecture
questions.explain: The Driver's awareness of task completion status is what allows this kind of automatic recovery.
